failure_modes: Reading a change of form as retreat and abandoning the strategy
Holding the reserve form too long and missing the moment it was needed
gloss: A life cycle is a set of tactics played under stress, not a fixed sequence of stages
invariants: Forms are selected by conditions, not by a predetermined order
What was learned in one form carries into the next
mechanism: An organism or agent holds several forms and switches between them according to environmental stress, all serving one overall strategy. The slime mould lives as single cells, aggregates into a collective body through {{self_organisation}} when food runs out, and releases spores as an option held in reserve. Failure in one form is a reason to change form, not to leave the game. The repertoire is {{meta_modularity}} applied to the body or organisation itself. Ending one instance and passing on what matters, as in {{generational_knowledge_transfer}}, is the same tactic at the scale of a lineage.
